text:
sophie: Quick smoke on ganymede-7b int4 bring-up for longform summarization. ran 1k-story slice, pushing numbers + a couple failure cases. thoughts on routing/canary?

kevin: link to raw figs?

sophie: paste of summary below (copied from notebook). TL;DR: ~42% token cost reduction vs float16, avg latency down 25%, but ROUGE-L drops 3.5 pts and hallucination rate up from 2.1% -> 5.9% on the dataset. examples: one where timeline items got swapped, another where entity name dropped.

sophie: ```
model        cost_per_1k_tokens  p95_latency_ms  rouge-l  halluc_rate
ganymede-7b-fp16    $0.20              180            46.8     2.1%
ganymede-7b-int4    $0.12              135            43.3     5.9%
%cost_saving ~40% latency_improve ~25% quality_loss -3.5pt
```

eval-bot: Automated eval summary: longform_coherence = -0.9 (z-score), entity_fidelity = -0.13 (relative). See /evals/3921234567/ganymede-int4-report (internal).

maria: 3.5pt ROUGE drop is high for core product summarization. but cost savings are nice. do we have per-slice signal? where is degradation concentrated (length, instruction type)?

sophie: degraded mainly on >800 token source docs and where multi-entity temporal ordering matters. short summaries (<150 src tokens) look identical.

aj: for GTN, longform customers matter. we can't surface int4 as default for those routes. propose routing by source_length and a quick quality proxy (e.g., logprob gap / repeat-token count).

kevin: agree. propose a hybrid: default int4 for small/medium requests, float16 fallback for >threshold or if proxy crosses threshold. canary math?

sophie: did quick unit-econ calc: assume avg interaction = 800 input + 200 output tokens. token cost numbers -> int4: $0.12 per 1k tokens, fp16: $0.20 per 1k. per-request cost int4 = $0.12*(1.0)= $0.096, fp16 = $0.16, saving ~$0.064 per request. at 100k monthly requests, ~$6.4k/mo. But if we route 30% to fp16 for longform / high-risk, savings down to ~$4.5k/mo.

maria: also include quality-cost of false positives (bad summaries). any metric to estimate customer impact? maybe downgrade score by engagement delta -> revenue impact. we should capture an eval-flag to label production failures and route back.

sophie: implementation sketch:
```yaml
routing_policy:
  - if src_tokens > 800: route: ganymede-7b-fp16
  - else if proxy_logprob_gap < -3.0: route: ganymede-7b-fp16
  - else: route: ganymede-7b-int4
canary:
  percent: 5%
  monitor: rouge-l_delta, hallucination_rate, latency_p95
  rollback_thresholds:
    rouge_drop: 1.0
    halluc_increase_pct: 200%
```

ops-bot: Deploy plan created: infra/route-configs#451. will schedule canary on dedicated pool tomorrow 03:00 UTC.

kevin: add tracing hooks to capture model_confidence proxy + p60/p95 lat. we want automated re-route if p95 > 300ms too.

maria: for GTN guidance writeup: recommend default = int4 for interactive short summaries, explicit product flag for "longer_document" -> fp16. include canary + auto-fallback. also propose an A/B to measure engagement impact for 30 days.

aj: sounds good. can we get a short scorecard for PMs? one-line recs + unit econ + risk level.

sophie: I'll draft the scorecard and PR: includes per-slice ROUGE, hallucination, latency, unit-cost numbers, and recommended routing policy. will include ~20 manual error examples for triage. cc @maria @kevin.

maria: :thumbsup: pls add a column in scorecard for mitigation complexity (low/med/high).

kevin: thanks. if we can keep canary at 5% and monitor, i'm comfortable rolling after 48h no regression.

sophie: will open thread PR + add dashboard tiles. follow-up doc link when ready.
